families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer matrices combined with retained acid and plasticising polar phases to preserve proton pathways into the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or bound polar phases support low-temperature fluid continuity in polymer films.
D3: biopolymer/polyol-like blends are plausibly less brittle than dry neat hosts under subambient operation.
D4: phosphoric-acid-containing eutectic or confined acid states are supported as non-crystallising proton-source environments.
D6: starch/chitosan/PVA provide dense hydrogen-bonding landscapes for hybrid proton transfer.
D7: chitosan and low-level phosphoric-acid strategies support acid/water retention.

families.family_description: One-dimensional mineral hosts confine and retain hydrated acid domains while guiding interconnected nanoscale transport pathways.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric acid is supported as a mobile proton source, including eutectic-like acid environments.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite nanotubes explicitly provide interconnected nanoconfinement.
D6: phosphoric acid supplies hydrogen-bond-mediated proton relay.
D7: fibrous/tubular clays are reported to reduce acid loss and improve retention.

families.family_description: Amorphous proton-bearing inorganic phases blended with hydrogen-bonding hosts aim to deliver continuous transport without crystallisation-driven disruption.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is directly described as an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D4: retained phosphoric-acid-like or protonated phosphate states avoid neat crystalline acid domains.
D6: phosphate networks and OH-rich polymers both provide dense donor/acceptor landscapes.
D7: confinement or network incorporation can retain the conducting phase, though some glass systems show stability caveats.

instances.composition_description: Chitosan-rich film blended with PVA, loaded with 1-D attapulgite and doped with retained phosphoric acid at moderate level.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-water and acid continuity within OH-rich film
nanoconfinement: 1-D clay may preserve interconnected acid channels
retention: chitosan-clay interactions may suppress phosphoric-acid loss
risk_flags: no direct subzero proof for this exact quaternary blend
excess acid may still plasticise too strongly or leach

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is reported as an acid-interacting scaffold aiding confinement and retention, and DES-containing chitosan films tolerate high water uptake without disintegration.
PVA contributes OH-mediated hydrogen bonding and compatibility in polysaccharide blends, analogously supporting proton-relay landscapes.
Attapulgite is directly reported to provide 1-D nanoconfinement and acid immobilisation in a proton-conducting composite.
Phosphoric acid is supported as a mobile proton source in complexed environments and as the hydrogen-bond-mediated conducting medium at low temperature.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy motif assembled from separately supported roles rather than a directly reported exact formulation. Novelty lies in combining biopolymer retention, PVA film flexibility, 1-D clay confinement, and phosphoric-acid conduction in one cold-targeted membrane.

instances.composition_description: Starch-PVA blend plasticised and protonated by a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep eutectic phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: eutectic phase may resist freezing better than neat water-rich acid
flexibility: plasticised starch/PVA matrix may remain less brittle below room temperature
proton_relay: dense OH network plus acid complex supports hybrid transport
risk_flags: eutectic uptake may over-soften the film
acid retention versus humidity cycling is not directly proven

element_evidence.reason: Starch is reported to provide dense hydrogen-bonding functionality and channel-like transport pathways in proton-conducting blends.
PVA supplies OH-rich hydrogen-bonding interactions that improve compatibility and plausibly sustain relay pathways.
Choline chloride is directly supported as the complexing partner in a ChCl/PA deep eutectic proton-carrier environment.
Phosphoric acid is supported both as the acid component of the eutectic and as a hydrogen-bond-mediated proton-conducting phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: The novelty is the transfer of a ChCl/PA eutectic motif into a starch/PVA OH-rich film aimed at subambient continuity. Evidence supports each role individually, but this exact combined membrane was not directly claimed in the pool.

instances.composition_description: Tubular halloysite host loaded with phosphoric acid as a confined proton-conducting phase.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: tubular lumen can localise the acid phase
retention: clay-acid interaction may reduce leaching
cold_window: confined acid may avoid bulk-like freezing behavior
risk_flags: standalone powder or brittle compact may need a binder for membrane use

element_evidence.reason: HNTs are directly described as hosting phosphoric acid with confinement and reduced leaching.
Phosphoric acid is supported as a mobile proton source and as the hydrogen-bond-mediated conducting phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a control because the PA@HNT motif is directly represented by the claim pool. It anchors the candidate set with one low-novelty benchmark for confined-acid transport.

instances.composition_description: Chitosan matrix embedding phosphoric-acid-loaded halloysite nanotubes to couple polymer retention with tubular confinement.
expected_properties: retention: chitosan plus HNTs may jointly suppress acid loss
nanostructure: dispersed tubes can create connected confined pathways
cold_window: bound acid-water domains are plausible within the composite
risk_flags: tube aggregation could break pathway continuity

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is evidenced as an acid-interacting scaffold with retention benefits and tolerance to hydrated/plasticised states.
HNTs directly provide phosphoric-acid confinement and reduced susceptibility to leaching.
Phosphoric acid is supported as the proton source and hydrogen-bond-mediated conducting phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: This candidate extends the proven PA@HNT confinement motif by embedding it in a chitosan retention scaffold. The combination is novel relative to the pool but built from directly compatible component-level claims.

instances.composition_description: Fine protonated phosphate-glass phase dispersed through a starch/PVA hydrogen-bonding film to form an amorphous hybrid proton reservoir.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous glass can provide non-crystalline proton domains
proton_relay: polymer OH groups may bridge inorganic and organic transport sites
retention: inorganic phase may reduce volatility of the conducting fraction
risk_flags: glass-polymer interfacial brittleness may emerge at high loading

element_evidence.reason: Protonated phosphate glass is directly described as amorphous and proton-conducting with strong hydrogen bonding, though retention/stability can be conditional.
Starch provides OH-rich channel-forming and hydrogen-bond-dense functionality that can analogously couple to the glass phase.
PVA contributes an OH-rich flexible film-forming network that can analogously bridge proton-relay sites around dispersed glass.

instances.novelty_rationale: The novelty is the hybridisation of an amorphous inorganic proton reservoir with a starch/PVA soft host to target continuity across 182–299 K. Evidence exists for each component role, but the integrated cold-oriented hybrid is not directly reported in the pool.
